record.paper_title: Open problems on classical de Sitter solutions
record.original_question: For classical 10-dimensional string backgrounds with a 4-dimensional de Sitter spacetime, D-brane sources, and orientifold sources, must every classical de Sitter solution that contains intersecting sources be perturbatively unstable, equivalently having at least one tachyonic 4-dimensional scalar mode?

evidence.quote:
Classical 10d string backgrounds with a 4d de Sitter space-time, D-brane and orientifold sources, are commonly believed to satisfy the following:
2. Classical de Sitter solutions with intersecting sources are unstable.
Conjecture 2 Classical de Sitter solutions with intersecting sources are unstable.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider classical ten-dimensional string backgrounds of type II supergravity whose spacetime is a warped product of four-dimensional de Sitter spacetime $dS_4$ with a six-dimensional internal manifold, and whose only localized sources are D$p$-branes and O$p$-orientifold planes (treated in the smeared or localized supergravity approximation, with the standard NSNS and RR field content satisfying the equations of motion and Bianchi identities). Say that such a solution "contains intersecting sources" if there exist at least two source stacks (D-branes and/or orientifolds) whose internal worldvolume directions are not all parallel, i.e. they wrap distinct, transversely-intersecting cycles in the internal manifold. A solution is called perturbatively unstable if the spectrum of four-dimensional scalar fluctuations around it contains at least one mode whose squared mass $m^2$ satisfies $m^2/H^2 < 0$ (a tachyonic mode), where $H$ is the de Sitter Hubble scale; equivalently, the slow-roll-type parameter $\eta_V = \min(\nabla^2 V)/V$ is negative at the critical point.

Prove or disprove: every classical de Sitter solution of the above form that contains intersecting sources is perturbatively unstable.
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is a conjecture supported empirically: all known classical de Sitter solutions with intersecting D-brane/orientifold sources (typically on group manifolds) are tachyonic, often with η_V < -1. Subsequent works (e.g. Andriot 2021 on tachyonic de Sitter solutions of 10d type II supergravities) develop sufficient conditions and identify a systematic tachyon under assumptions, but no general proof exists. The conjecture is therefore still open.

status_evidence.title: Tachyonic de Sitter Solutions of 10d Type II Supergravities
status_evidence.snippet: Develops three methods giving sufficient conditions for a tachyon under assumptions, aiming at proving its systematic presence.
status_evidence.claim: No general proof; only sufficient conditions under assumptions.

status_evidence.title: Classical de Sitter solutions in three dimensions without tachyons?
status_evidence.snippet: Explores whether tachyon-free classical de Sitter solutions exist, indicating the question of systematic instability remains under investigation.
status_evidence.claim: Status of the instability conjecture is still being explored.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on classical de Sitter solutions
status_evidence.snippet: Lists as Conjecture 2 that classical de Sitter solutions with intersecting sources are unstable.
